_meta.description: Document-rules config for replication — Plaintiff's replication / rejoinder to defendant's Written Statement under Order VIII R.9 CPC
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Replication is restricted to dealing with new facts in WS; not re-statement of plaint.

title: Replication / Rejoinder to Written Statement (Order VIII R.9 CPC)

fields.label: Leave of court obtained for replication (Order VIII R.9)
List of NEW facts / additional pleas in WS that require reply (not facts already covered in plaint)
Reply to set-off claim by defendant (if any)
Written statement to defendant's counter-claim (Order VIII R.6E)
Para-wise response to defendant's additional pleas / new facts
Response to defendant's preliminary objections (jurisdiction, limitation, maintainability)
Additional documents relied upon (only relating to new matters)
Confirm replication does not introduce new cause of action or relief (only addresses new defence facts)

mandatory_clauses.name: Leave of Court Recital — Order VIII R.9
mandatory_clauses.description: Replication is filed with leave of court (or pursuant to court direction)

mandatory_clauses.name: Scope Statement
mandatory_clauses.description: Confirms replication is confined to dealing with new pleas in WS, not re-iterating plaint

mandatory_clauses.name: Reply to Preliminary Objections
mandatory_clauses.description: Response to maintainability / jurisdiction / limitation pleas raised in WS

mandatory_clauses.name: Reply to New Facts / Additional Pleas in WS
mandatory_clauses.description: Specific reply to each new fact pleaded in WS — admit / deny / counter

mandatory_clauses.name: Written Statement to Counter-claim (Order VIII R.6E)
mandatory_clauses.description: Where defendant has filed counter-claim, plaintiff files WS in reply within time fixed; replication may incorporate

mandatory_clauses.name: No New Cause of Action / Relief
mandatory_clauses.description: Replication cannot introduce new cause of action or expand reliefs beyond plaint

mandatory_clauses.name: Prayer
mandatory_clauses.description: Reiterate reliefs sought in plaint with reference to replication

mandatory_clauses.name: Affidavit in support — Order VI R.15(4)

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {plaintiff_name}, son/daughter/wife of {plaintiff_father_name}, aged about {plaintiff_age} years, resident of {plaintiff_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above Replication are true and correct to my personal knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Plaintiff

promptInstructions: Draft a Replication / Rejoinder strictly under Order VIII Rule 9 CPC.

Order VIII R.9 CPC: 'No pleading subsequent to the written statement of a defendant other than by way of defence to set-off or counter-claim shall be presented except by the leave of the Court and upon such terms as the Court thinks fit; but the Court may at any time require a written statement or additional written statement from any of the parties and fix a time of not more than thirty days for presenting the same.'
KEY PRINCIPLE — Replication is NOT a matter of right. It requires LEAVE of court (or court's own direction). Many courts insist on a formal application for leave before accepting replication.

SCOPE — Replication is strictly LIMITED to dealing with new pleas / new facts introduced by defendant in WS. It is NOT an opportunity to: (a) re-state or amplify plaint; (b) introduce new cause of action; (c) expand reliefs; (d) cure defects in plaint (those require amendment under Order VI R.17).
Cite: Manmohan Singh v. Punjab National Bank (2008) — replication confined to new facts in WS; cannot be vehicle for new pleadings.
Cite: Anant Construction (P) Ltd v. Ram Niwas (1994) 56 DLT 547 (Del HC) — replication permissible only where WS introduces new facts requiring reply; plaintiff cannot bring in fresh cause of action.
Para 1: Cause title and suit reference.
Para 2: Recite that replication is filed with leave of this Hon'ble Court granted on [date] on application dated [date] / pursuant to direction of court.

Para 3: Scope statement — 'This replication is confined to dealing with the new facts and pleas raised in the Written Statement dated ____ filed by the Defendant. The Plaintiff reiterates and reaffirms the averments in the Plaint and does not seek to alter, add to or modify the cause of action or the reliefs sought therein.'
Para 4 onwards: Reply to PRELIMINARY OBJECTIONS in WS — point-by-point response to maintainability / jurisdiction / limitation / cause of action pleas.
Para X onwards: Reply to NEW FACTS pleaded by defendant in WS — admit / deny / counter for each new factual allegation.
Where defendant has pleaded payment, release, discharge, fraud, illegality etc. — these require specific reply.
Where defendant has pleaded SET-OFF (Order VIII R.6) — file reply showing set-off claim untenable.

Where defendant has filed COUNTER-CLAIM (Order VIII R.6A-6G) — Order VIII R.6E mandates plaintiff to file written statement in answer to counter-claim within time fixed by court. This is technically a separate document from replication, but commonly incorporated.
Para final: Reaffirm plaint averments and reliefs.
Tone: precise, restrained. Do not be repetitive. Confine to what is genuinely new.
Verification — Order VI R.15.
Affidavit in support — Order VI R.15(4).
Note: in Commercial Courts under CCA 2015, the procedure is somewhat streamlined and statement of truth applies (Order VI R.15A). Replication is still subject to leave under Order VIII R.9.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

filing_checklist: Replication (original + copies for defendant and court)
Application under Order VIII R.9 CPC for leave to file replication (if not already granted)
Affidavit in support of replication (Order VI R.15(4))
Statement of Truth (if Commercial Court — Order VI R.15A)
Additional documents relating only to new matters (if any) with list
WS to counter-claim (Order VIII R.6E) — if defendant filed counter-claim
Court fee — generally nominal / fixed for subsequent pleadings (refer state Schedule)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: leave_application_filed must be true (leave is mandatory under Order VIII R.9)
new_facts_in_ws must not be empty — replication is restricted to dealing with new facts
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Manmohan Singh v. Punjab National Bank — Replication scope is limited to new facts in WS
Anant Construction (P) Ltd v. Ram Niwas (1994) 56 DLT 547 — Replication cannot introduce new pleadings; confined to WS new facts
Mahabir Prasad Jain v. Ganga Singh AIR 1999 SC 3873 — Subsequent pleadings only with leave
Gian Chand v. York Exports Ltd (2014) 14 SCC 729 — Replication / rejoinder restricted scope; not amendment substitute
Sangram Singh v. Election Tribunal AIR 1955 SC 425 — Pleadings principles and fair opportunity
